@@U02393@@
Good, but don’t stop there; describe him precisely.

@@U02395@@
How does one describe dignity? That healthy moon of a face and full mouth, the full-blown cheeks beneath a handsome turban, and luxuriously comfortable in his pleated robe! And what’s to be said of his noble bearing! He looks every inch the ruler!

@@U02397@@
He’s 普路托斯, god of Wealth, come in splendor to your Emperor who desires mightily to see him.

@@U02399@@
And you? Tell us of yourself. Who are you?

@@U02401@@
I am Prodigality. I am Poetry. The spendthrift who achieves fulfillment by squandering what is most personal to him. Like 普路托斯, I am immeasurably rich; I enliven his dances, his feasts and festivals, and what he lacks I supply.
translation:
@@U02393@@
很好，但不要就此止步；准确地描述他。

@@U02395@@
怎样形容一个人的尊严呢？健康的月亮般的脸庞和饱满的嘴巴，漂亮的头巾下丰满的脸颊，穿着褶皱长袍的奢华舒适！更何况他的高贵举止呢！他看起来浑身都是统治者！

@@U02397@@
他是普路托斯，财富之神，带着光彩来到你们的皇帝面前，他非常渴望见到他。

@@U02399@@
你呢？告诉我们你自己吧。你是谁？

@@U02401@@
我是挥霍者。我是诗。挥霍者通过挥霍对他来说最私人的东西来获得满足。像普路托斯一样，我非常富有；我使他的舞蹈、他的盛宴和节日充满活力，他所缺乏的我也供应。
